text:
morgan: quick async check — onboarding opt-13b-ql. We pushed weights to s3://redwood-models/opt/13b-q4_0/2026-03-10/ - can someone confirm tokenizer mapping? I'm seeing different EOS handling in the tokenizer that breaks prefix caching on a few prompts.

alex: I pulled the weights and ran the tokenizer against our canonical prompt set. It's using a byte-level BPE variant and EOS is only appended on generation by default. If inputs have trailing whitespace they tokenize differently which invalidates prefix cache. PR #472 adds an input normalization step. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/472

tara: quick config sanity check — continuous_batcher defaults look aggressive for this model. We're seeing high p95 latency when max_tokens=1024 and batch_timeout_ms=20. Any recommended knobs?

paul: suggested provisional config (trying to balance throughput/latency):
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  batch_timeout_ms: 15
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_payloads: 32
caching:
  prefix_cache_enabled: true
  prefix_cache_max_tokens: 512
  prefix_cache_ttl_ms: 300000
scheduler:
  slot_limit: 8
  max_inflight_per_model: 64
max_tokens: 1024
```
This reduces batching latency while keeping decent token amortization. Also set KV cache eviction to LRU for now.

ci-bot: preflight: model load SUCCESS on staging cluster, but detected shard placement warning: over-allocated on node gpu-12 by 1 shard.

sam: moved shard from gpu-12 -> gpu-08 and restarted the agent on gpu-08. Did not change scheduler slot_limit yet. For safety set max_inflight_per_model to 64 and slot_limit to 8 while we observe.

alex: re: tokenizer quirks — temporary workaround is to canonicalize inputs in the client SDK: strip trailing whitespace and force-add EOS token in the pre-tokenize hook. I'll push a small wrapper to the js/python SDKs and attach tests.

tara: I'll run a perf sweep on staging with alex's canonicalizer + paul's batcher config. ETA ~45m, will post p50/p95/p99 and CPU impact.

morgan: thanks. If perf looks stable, plan: roll to dedicated-alpha with a 10% canary and auto-fallback to smaller quantized variant. Add a canary route config and a health check threshold (p95 < 300ms).

paul: one more note — prefix cache max_tokens=512 is conservative; if soak shows lower mem pressure we can bump to 1024 for better hit rate. Keep TTL at 5m for now.

tara: results: after canonicalizer + batch_timeout_ms=15 -> p50 28ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms on staging. Tokenizer workers CPU up ~12%. No OOMs. Running 1h soak now.

morgan: great — tag the PRs (alex: tokenizer wrapper, paul: config change) and I'll open rollout ticket for dedicated-alpha canary. Also create a follow-up to revisit prefix_cache_max_tokens after 1h soak.
